Graduation dates.

Twenty-five years of experience.

Your full address.

Old jobs that have absolutely nothing to do with the role you're applying for.

None of it helps you get hired.

In this video, we break down why you should only include what's relevant, why the last 10 years are usually enough, and how to make your resume easier for recruiters and hiring managers to read without giving away information they don't need.

Your resume isn't there to tell your life story.

It's there to get you an interview.
title: STOP GIVING AWAY YOUR AGE ON YOUR RESUME!
